sourcedFrom: Ruger American Rimfire Bolt-Action Rifle Instruction Manual — PM300 (2016)
cleanIntro: Bolt out is all routine cleaning needs, and Ruger says so plainly. Taking the barrelled action out of the stock is documented too, on the Deep Clean path.

steps.title: Safe direction, safety on
steps.action: Keep the rifle pointed in a safe direction and put the safety in the "Safe" position if the firing pin is cocked.
steps.prose: Whether it is cocked decides whether the safety will engage at all.
steps.quote: Keep the rifle pointed in a safe direction!
steps.cite: Ruger American Rimfire Bolt-Action Rifle Instruction Manual — PM300 — Disassembly, step 1, p.11
steps.warn: Rifle must be unloaded prior to disassembly.

steps.title: Chamber and magazine empty
steps.action: Check that the chamber and magazine are empty, then remove the magazine.
steps.quote: CHECK TO BE CERTAIN THAT THE CHAMBER AND MAGAZINE ARE EMPTY. Remove the magazine.
steps.cite: Ruger American Rimfire Bolt-Action Rifle Instruction Manual — PM300 — Disassembly, step 2, p.11

steps.title: Bolt out — and that is the routine strip
steps.action: Open the bolt and pull it rearward while pressing the rear of the bolt stop. On a right-handed rifle the stop is on the left of the receiver; on a left-handed rifle it is on the right.
steps.prose: Ruger states outright that this is as far as routine cleaning goes.
steps.quote: This is as far as you need to dismantle the rifle for a routine cleaning. It is rarely necessary to proceed further.
steps.cite: Ruger American Rimfire Bolt-Action Rifle Instruction Manual — PM300 — Disassembly, step 3, p.11

deepSteps.title: Barrelled action out of the stock
deepSteps.action: Loosen and remove the two hex-head screws in the bottom of the stock, then lift the barrelled action out.
deepSteps.prose: Two screws, and note how they were torqued — a bolt rifle’s accuracy lives in how the action sits back down.
deepSteps.quote: Loosen and remove the two hex-head screws in the bottom of the stock. Lift the barreled-action out of the stock.
deepSteps.cite: Ruger American Rimfire Bolt-Action Rifle Instruction Manual — PM300 — Disassembly, step 4, p.11

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Solvent patch, correctly sized brush, then dry patches until clean
Rimfire fouling is waxy and builds fast — the chamber needs as much attention as the bore
Clean from the chamber end where the design allows

cleaning.name: BOLT / ACTION
tasks: Wipe the bolt face and around the extractor
Clean the receiver raceways and the magazine well
Light oil on bearing surfaces only

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES
tasks: Wipe magazine bodies dry — no oil where ammunition sits

reassembly: Return the bolt with the bolt stop depressed, then release the stop.
If the action was out of the stock, seat it and tighten both hex-head screws evenly.
fncheck: With the magazine out and chamber confirmed empty, check the safety blocks the trigger and the bolt cycles and locks cleanly.
